notes: Wikidata SPARQL by object class (wdt:P31 / wdt:P31/wdt:P279*), filtered to items with an image (P18) AND an enwiki sitelink, plus the BBC/British Museum 'A History of the World in 100 Objects' list. See tools/fame/HARVEST_OBJECTS_V2.md.
Does not touch universe_objects.json, current_inventory.json or any data/*.json file -- for human review / a later merge pass into build_universe_objects.py only.
'specialist'-tagged candidates were dropped entirely per spec; only household_name/enthusiast survive into this file.

variety_trim.rationale: Product-owner steer (25 Jul 2026): prioritise variety of subject matter over raw volume; trim the categories that already have some representation (ship/painting/sculpture/vehicle) before ever touching the zero-representation categories this harvest exists to fill (clothing, tool, weapon, coin, musical_instrument, jewellery, furniture, machine, archaeological_find). Raised the sitelinks bar to >=22 for kind in {vehicle, ship, painting, sculpture} only; every other kind is untouched at its original >=15 (or no) floor.

manual_cleanup.rationale: Post-harvest manual audit found several real, systemic contamination patterns not caught by the automated quality filter: (1) a Wikidata subclass-chain quirk (dome/headgear-shaped roofs apparently mis-modelled as a headgear subclass) pulled >100 ground-based astronomical OBSERVATORY BUILDINGS into the 'clothing' bucket; (2) a handful of medieval military-religious ORDERS (Knights Templar/Hospitaller, Teutonic Order) were classed as 'clothing' (they are organizations, not garments); (3) several broadcast towers, a museum building, an ancient cistern and two excavated buildings leaked into machine/tool/sculpture/archaeological_find; (4) the how100 wikitext parser's first_wikilink() heuristic grabs the FIRST wikilink in an object cell, which is often a culture/dynasty/deity/person/material modifier rather than the actual named object (e.g. '[[Mummy]] of [[Hornedjitef]]' -> picked 'Mummy' instead of the actual named mummy, 'Hornedjitef'); (5) a few non-physical software/app/video-game articles and one mythical object (Holy Grail) were instance-of a harvested class; (6) a handful of extremely generic modern mass-produced-item articles (Computer, Microwave oven, Belt, Chain...) with no distinct story, which the brief explicitly says to reject. All removed by exact QID/title match or, for the how100 parser bug, by how100_number -- see tools/fame/HARVEST_OBJECTS_V2.md.
